assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: the report builder and SQL window check your work and explain what is wrong.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Build the channel view, write the measurement plan and findings and pass the final assessment to finish the course.

faq.q: Does this connect to my own GA4 property?
faq.a: No. The lessons use a built-in sample of a small learning site, so you can practise without a website or a Google account. Everything you build runs in your browser.
They are described step by step with listings and examples, because the interface changes often and needs a real property. Check Google's current documentation for exact menu names.

faq.q: Does Google Tag Manager or BigQuery run here?
faq.a: No. They are explained, and the SQL labs query the same traffic as a flat events table, the shape of a BigQuery export, so the thinking carries over.
Comfort with basic percentages. SQL for Data & Business in this category helps for the SQL labs.
Finishing every module and the final assessment marks the course complete on your GrowQR profile. It is not a Google certification.

activities.title: The purchase funnel
activities.objective: Count a funnel with distinct sessions and a window function.
activities.scenario: Count the funnel: for the steps view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout and purchase, return `event_name`, `sessions` (distinct sessions that had the event) and `pct_of_views` (sessions as a percentage of the view_item step, one decimal). Show the steps in funnel order.
steps: Filter the four events and count COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) per event_name in a CTE, with a step number from CASE.
Divide by FIRST_VALUE(sessions) OVER (ORDER BY step) times 100.0.

checks.label: Your query runs without an error
checks.hint: Press Run query and read any message under the editor: it names the problem.
checks.explain: A query that does not run cannot be checked. The message tells you which word or column it could not understand.

checks.label: It uses COUNT(DISTINCT session_id)
checks.hint: The task needs COUNT(DISTINCT session_id). Think about which clause does that job.
checks.explain: COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) is the tool built for this part of the task.

checks.label: It uses FIRST_VALUE
checks.hint: The task needs FIRST_VALUE. Think about which clause does that job.
checks.explain: FIRST_VALUE is the tool built for this part of the task.

checks.label: It returns the right rows and columns
checks.hint: Compare the number of rows and columns you get with what the task describes, then check your conditions.
checks.explain: A funnel counts distinct sessions at each step, because one session can fire the same event several times. FIRST_VALUE gives the top of the funnel to divide by, and the CASE orders the steps.
